tracker.description: Space Telemax2. Big items = Goal list (task_type Goal); each goal's tickets are its linked tasks. Sprints = lists 'Sprint N (m/d - m/d)' in folder Sprint 2026, 2 weeks; a closed sprint's dashboard is final. Done = deployed to prod / Closed / ready for production; deployed to staging = dev done awaiting verification + release.

rules: Sprint counts follow the sprint dashboard: top-level tickets only (no subtasks); completed = status Closed (ClickUp status type 'closed'). 'deployed to prod' / 'ready for production' are shown separately as released / ready for release, never as completed.
Do not report sprint totals, completion rate or carry-over: unfinished tickets are moved to the next sprint list and keep no sprint history. Report completed (and cancelled) only.

Sprint 27–29 history = PM's figures from the previous report (completed 27 / 19 / 17; tickets per member ~5 / ~5 / ~3; production bugs 5 / — / 8; milestones 50% / 75% / —; expected ~20 per sprint from Sprint 30). The PM's earlier manual counts are authoritative — do not recount them.

Sprint comparison: Mermaid bar chart of completed tickets per sprint from Sprint 27, with a line for the velocity baseline (mean completed from Sprint 27 to the last ended sprint). Show the previous report's forecast vs actual.
Tickets per member counts developers only — Tony, Kelvin/KhanhND, Darius/DungVV, David Dany, Jim Francinilla. QA (MinhNT) and infra (NgaNQ) are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
Goals: the PM picks the goals each run; every goal not picked goes in an 'Other goals' table with name and status only — no due date.
Goal progress counts the lowest-level tickets linked to the goal (cancelled excluded) and shows Done / Dev done / Open counts plus % done and % including dev done. 'deployed to staging' = Dev done.
Goal status from its tickets: all released → Done; all built but some not yet released → Dev done. If the goal card status disagrees with its tickets, ask the PM instead of choosing.
Highlights: every item links to its ticket. Never write a generic item ('production bugs', 'issues fixed', 'umbrella') — read the ticket description and subtasks and say in one line what was fixed.

Team focus section (per developer), grouped by goal: one row per goal the developer owns or that one of their running-sprint tickets belongs to (ticket ∈ goal = the ticket, its parent or its subtask is linked to the goal; mark goals owned by someone else, and owned goals with no sprint ticket), then a 'Not in a goal' row for their other tickets. Columns: in progress / review / staging vs not started / on hold. A subtask is listed as its parent ticket, with its open subtasks summarised. Leave out done/Closed items and the shared 'PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT' task. Add an Unassigned row.
Goal 'Clean up unused services' (cost optimisation) is shown as TBU until the Azure cost figures are verified — do not use the Azure resource sheet summary.
Anything not confirmed by the PM (reasons, ETAs, wording for the client) stays as a [PM: …] placeholder; the report is a draft for the PM to review, and the e-mail is printed as text, never sent.

Goals are aligned with sprints and a goal can span several sprints: add a 'Goals across sprints' table — per goal, its tickets closed in each sprint (by close date), a separate column for released tickets with no close date (never guessed into a sprint), open incl. dev done, planned sprints (goal start → due) and the actual span. Flag planned-vs-actual gaps and missing/odd goal dates.

Goals were introduced in September 2026. For sprints before or alongside them, big tickets (closed top-level tickets with ≥2 real subtasks, QC/deployment helpers not counted) count as goals: list them in a 'Before goals — big items' table per sprint with what they contained, and note any that should be linked to a goal.
